questions.subject: ANH
questions.q:
Read the following passage and mark the letter A, B, C, or D to indicate the best answer to each question.

Last summer, 16-year-old Linh decided to spend her holiday differently. Instead of staying at home playing video games, she joined a volunteer group that teaches English to children in a mountain village. At first, Linh felt nervous because she had never taught anyone before. However, the children's bright smiles quickly melted her worries away.

Every morning, Linh and her friends prepared simple lessons with songs and games. The children, aged 6 to 10, were eager to learn although they had few books. In the afternoons, the volunteers helped repair the small village school and planted trees around it.

After one month, Linh returned home with unforgettable memories. She realized that volunteering had taught her as much as she had taught the children. She learned to be patient, confident, and grateful for what she has. 'I used to think holidays were for resting,' Linh said, 'but now I know they can also be for giving.'

Linh's story shows that young people can make a real difference. You do not need to be rich or famous to help others - you just need a kind heart and a little time.

What is the main idea of the passage?
options: A. Why video games are bad for teenagers
B. How to teach English to mountain children
C. Why Linh felt nervous at first
D. How Linh spent her summer holiday volunteering
questions.explain: Cả bài kể về kỳ nghỉ đi tình nguyện dạy tiếng Anh của Linh và bài học rút ra.

questions.q:
Read the following passage and mark the letter A, B, C, or D to indicate the best answer to each question.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing the way students learn around the world. In many schools, AI-powered apps now help students practise English, solve maths problems, and even write essays. Supporters say that AI makes learning more personal because it can adjust lessons to each student's level. A student who is weak in grammar, for instance, will receive more grammar exercises, while a stronger student moves on to harder tasks.

However, not everyone welcomes this change. Some teachers worry that students may depend too much on technology and stop thinking for themselves. If an AI app always gives the correct answer, students might not learn how to solve problems on their own. Every year, the world uses about 500 billion plastic bags. Most of them are used for just a few minutes, yet they can last for hundreds of years in the environment. In Vietnam, plastic bags from markets and shops end up in rivers and finally in the sea, harming fish and other sea creatures.

The good news is that change is possible. Many young people have started bringing cloth bags when they go shopping. Some shops now offer paper bags or charge extra for plastic ones. These small steps are making a big difference.

questions.subject: ANH
questions.q:
Read the following passage and mark the letter A, B, C, or D to indicate the best answer to each question.

Since 2020, working from home has become a popular trend around the world. Thanks to the internet, millions of people can now do their jobs without going to an office. Supporters of this trend point to clear benefits. Workers save time and money on travel, and they can arrange their own schedules. Many also say they feel less stressed without noisy offices and long commutes.

Companies benefit too. Businesses can rent smaller offices and spend less on electricity and equipment. Some studies even show that people working from home complete more tasks than those in offices, mainly because there are fewer interruptions.

However, working from home is not perfect. Many workers feel lonely because they miss chatting with colleagues. It can also be hard to separate work and rest when the office is your bedroom. Parents with small children often find it difficult to concentrate during the day.

Experts believe the future will combine both styles. Many companies now let employees work from home two or three days a week and come to the office on other days. This mixed model, called hybrid working, may offer the best of both worlds: the freedom of home and the energy of teamwork.

Whether at home or in the office, what matters most is finding a healthy balance between work and life.

What is the passage mainly about?
options: A. How to find a job online
B. The history of the internet
C. Why offices are always noisy
D. The benefits and drawbacks of working from home
questions.explain: Bài trình bày lợi ích, hạn chế của làm việc tại nhà và mô hình kết hợp.

In crowded cities, finding space for trees is difficult. However, some creative architects have found a clever solution: growing gardens on rooftops. These 'green roofs' are becoming popular in many countries, including Vietnam.

A green roof is covered with soil and plants instead of concrete. It offers several benefits. First, plants absorb rainwater, which reduces flooding in the rainy season. Second, green roofs keep buildings cooler in summer, so people use less air conditioning. Third, they provide homes for birds and insects in the middle of the city.

In Ho Chi Minh City, a primary school has turned its rooftop into a vegetable garden. Students grow tomatoes, herbs, and beans there. They learn about nature while producing fresh food for their lunch. 'Our garden makes the school more beautiful and cooler,' says 11-year-old Bao.

Experts believe green roofs could change city life in the future. Although building them costs money at first, the long-term benefits for the environment and people's health are worth it.

What is the main idea of the passage?
options: B. How to build a concrete roof
C. Why cities have no trees
D. The benefits of rooftop gardens in cities
questions.explain: Cả bài giới thiệu vườn trên mái nhà và các lợi ích của nó.

questions.subject: ANH
questions.q:
Read the following passage and mark the letter A, B, C, or D to indicate the best answer to each question.

Social media is now a central part of teenagers' lives. Platforms like TikTok, Instagram, and Facebook allow young people to connect with friends, share photos, and follow their favourite stars. For many teens, checking social media is the first thing they do in the morning and the last thing at night.

There are clear positives. Social media helps teens keep in touch with distant friends and discover new interests. It can also be a powerful tool for learning: many students follow educational channels that explain lessons in fun ways. During difficult times, online communities can offer comfort and support.

However, researchers warn about the negative side. Spending too much time online can lead to poor sleep and less physical activity. Worse, some teens compare themselves with the 'perfect' lives they see online and feel unhappy about their own. Cyberbullying - hurtful messages sent through phones or computers - is another serious problem that can damage young people's confidence.

So what should teens do? Experts suggest a balanced approach. They advise turning off notifications while studying, avoiding phones before bed, and remembering that online images are often edited and unrealistic. Parents are also encouraged to talk openly with their children about their online experiences.

Used wisely, social media can be a helpful friend rather than a harmful enemy. The key is to control it before it controls you.

What is the passage mainly about?
options: A. The pros and cons of social media for teenagers
C. How to become famous on TikTok
D. Why parents dislike the internet
questions.explain: Bài trình bày mặt tích cực, tiêu cực của mạng xã hội và lời khuyên dùng cân bằng.

Read the following passage and mark the letter A, B, C, or D to indicate the best answer to each question.

Social media is now a central part of teenagers' lives. Platforms like TikTok, Instagram, and Facebook allow young people to connect with friends, share photos, and follow their favourite stars. For many teens, checking social media is the first thing they do in the morning and the last thing at night.

There are clear positives. Social media helps teens keep in touch with distant friends and discover new interests. It can also be a powerful tool for learning: many students follow educational channels that explain lessons in fun ways. During difficult times, online communities can offer comfort and support.

However, researchers warn about the negative side. Spending too much time online can lead to poor sleep and less physical activity. Worse, some teens compare themselves with the 'perfect' lives they see online and feel unhappy about their own. Cyberbullying - hurtful messages sent through phones or computers - is another serious problem that can damage young people's confidence.

So what should teens do? Experts suggest a balanced approach. They advise turning off notifications while studying, avoiding phones before bed, and remembering that online images are often edited and unrealistic. Parents are also encouraged to talk openly with their children about their online experiences.

Used wisely, social media can be a helpful friend rather than a harmful enemy. The key is to control it before it controls you.

Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a negative effect of social media?
questions.explain: Bài nêu mất ngủ, ít vận động, bắt nạt mạng - không nhắc hóa đơn điện thoại cao hơn.

Read the following passage and mark the letter A, B, C, or D to indicate the best answer to each question.

As traditional energy sources like coal and oil run out, the world is turning to renewable energy. Solar power and wind power are the two most popular choices. Unlike fossil fuels, they do not pollute the air and will never run out.

Vietnam has great potential for renewable energy. With long coastlines and strong sunshine, the country can produce a large amount of clean electricity. In recent years, many solar farms have appeared in central and southern Vietnam. These farms turn sunlight into electricity for thousands of homes.

Wind power is also growing. Wind turbines along the coast spin day and night, creating power even when the sun is down. Experts say combining solar and wind energy can provide stable electricity all year round.

However, there are challenges. Building solar farms and wind turbines requires a lot of money and land. The equipment also needs regular maintenance. Despite these difficulties, most experts agree that renewable energy is the future. It protects the environment and helps countries become less dependent on imported fuels.

What is the main idea of the passage?
options: A. How to build a solar farm
B. Why coal and oil are cheap
C. Renewable energy as the future of power
questions.explain: Cả bài nói về năng lượng tái tạo: tiềm năng, lợi ích, thách thức và tương lai.

Read the following passage and mark the letter A, B, C, or D to indicate the best answer to each question.

Fast fashion refers to cheap clothes that are quickly produced to follow the latest trends. Brands release new collections every few weeks, encouraging people to buy more and throw away old clothes. While low prices attract shoppers, the real cost of fast fashion is much higher than it seems.

The environmental damage is serious. The fashion industry uses huge amounts of water: producing one cotton T-shirt requires about 2,700 liters of water. Chemical dyes from factories pollute rivers in many countries. Worse, most discarded clothes end up in landfills, where synthetic fabrics take hundreds of years to break down.

Workers also suffer. To keep prices low, some factories pay very low wages and force employees to work long hours in unsafe conditions. Many of these workers are young women in developing countries.

Fortunately, attitudes are changing. More young people now buy second-hand clothes, swap outfits with friends, or choose brands that treat workers fairly. Some designers are creating clothes from recycled materials.

Fashion should be fun, but it should not cost the earth. By thinking before we buy, each of us can help make the fashion industry cleaner and fairer.

What is the passage mainly about?
options: D. The hidden costs of fast fashion
questions.explain: Bài phơi bày chi phí môi trường và xã hội ẩn sau thời trang nhanh giá rẻ.

Learning a second language opens doors to new opportunities. Bilingual people - those who speak two languages - often find it easier to get good jobs. Many international companies prefer employees who can communicate with foreign partners.

Research shows that bilingualism also benefits the brain. People who regularly use two languages tend to have better memory and focus. They are often quicker at solving problems because their brains practise switching between languages every day. Some studies even suggest that bilingualism can delay memory loss in old age.

For Vietnamese students, English is the most popular second language. It gives access to knowledge, scholarships, and global friendships. However, experts remind learners not to forget their mother tongue. Vietnamese carries the culture and identity of the nation.

Twelve-year-old An, who speaks both Vietnamese and English fluently, says: 'English helps me explore the world, but Vietnamese helps me understand who I am.' His words remind us that each language is a key to a different world.

What is the main idea of the passage?
options: A. How to learn English fast
B. The benefits of being bilingual

Humans have dreamed of travelling to space for centuries. In 1969, that dream came true when American astronauts first walked on the Moon. Since then, space exploration has advanced rapidly, with robots exploring Mars and telescopes photographing distant galaxies.

Today, space exploration is no longer limited to governments. Private companies are building reusable rockets, making space travel cheaper than ever. Some even plan to take tourists on trips around the Moon in the near future. Meanwhile, scientists are searching for signs of life on other planets.

Space research also improves life on Earth. Technologies first developed for space, such as water filters and solar panels, are now used in our daily lives. Satellite images help farmers predict weather and fishermen find fish. GPS, which guides millions of drivers every day, would not exist without satellites.

However, space exploration faces criticism. Critics argue that the money spent on space could solve problems like hunger and disease on Earth. Supporters respond that exploring space inspires young people to study science and that the benefits will multiply in the future.

Whether we look up at the stars with wonder or with doubt, one thing is certain: humanity's journey into space has only just begun.

What is the passage mainly about?
options: A. The history of private companies
B. How to become an astronaut
C. Why the Moon is important
D. The development and benefits of space exploration

Read the following passage and mark the letter A, B, C, or D to indicate the best answer to each question.

Traffic jams are a daily headache in big cities like Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City. Thousands of motorbikes fill the streets every morning, causing pollution and wasting time. One effective solution is to improve public transport, especially buses.

Modern buses are comfortable, cheap, and environmentally friendly. A single bus can carry 50 passengers, replacing about 30 motorbikes on the road. This means less traffic and cleaner air. Many cities around the world, such as Singapore and Seoul, have excellent bus systems that millions of people use every day.

In Vietnam, bus services are improving. New buses with air conditioning and free Wi-Fi have appeared in several cities. Some routes now use electric buses, which produce no smoke at all. However, buses still face problems: they are often late during rush hours, and many stops lack shelters.

Experts suggest that if buses become faster and more reliable, more people will choose them over motorbikes. Building separate bus lanes and adding more routes are important steps. With better public transport, our cities can become cleaner, quieter, and more pleasant places to live.

What is the main idea of the passage?
options: B. How to drive a bus
C. Improving buses to solve traffic problems
D. The history of public transport
questions.explain: Cả bài bàn giải pháp kẹt xe: cải thiện xe buýt công cộng.

questions.subject: ANH
questions.q:
Read the following passage and mark the letter A, B, C, or D to indicate the best answer to each question.

Online learning has grown rapidly in recent years. With just a smartphone and internet connection, students can now attend classes, watch lectures, and submit homework from home. During the pandemic, millions of Vietnamese students studied online for months, proving that learning does not always require a classroom.

Online learning offers clear advantages. Students can study at their own pace, replaying difficult lessons as many times as they need. It also saves time and money on travel. For students in remote areas, online courses provide access to good teachers they could never meet otherwise.

However, learning online has drawbacks. Without classmates nearby, some students feel isolated and lose motivation. It is also harder for teachers to check whether students are truly paying attention. Technical problems, such as weak internet signals, can interrupt lessons at important moments.

To succeed in online learning, students need self-discipline. Experts recommend creating a quiet study corner, following a fixed schedule, and taking regular breaks. Parents can help by encouraging their children and limiting distractions.

Looking ahead, education will likely mix online and traditional methods. This blended approach combines the flexibility of technology with the warmth of human interaction, giving students the best of both worlds.

What is the passage mainly about?
options: A. The advantages and challenges of online learning
B. How to buy a smartphone
C. The history of the pandemic
questions.explain: Bài trình bày ưu điểm, hạn chế của học trực tuyến và hướng kết hợp.

However, learning online has drawbacks. Without classmates nearby, some students feel isolated and lose motivation. It is also harder for teachers to check whether students are truly paying attention. Technical problems, such as weak internet signals, can interrupt lessons at important moments.

Bees play a vital role in nature. They carry pollen from flower to flower, helping plants produce fruits and seeds. Without bees, many of the foods we love - apples, strawberries, and coffee - would disappear.

Sadly, bee numbers are falling around the world. Scientists believe several factors are responsible. Pesticides used on farms can poison bees. Climate change disrupts the timing of flowering, leaving bees without food. Diseases spread quickly among bee colonies kept close together.

The decline of bees affects humans directly. Farmers may produce less food, and prices could rise. Some regions already hire people to pollinate fruit trees by hand - a slow and costly job that bees once did for free.

Fortunately, we can help. Planting flowers that bloom in different seasons gives bees food all year. Avoiding pesticides in gardens protects them. In cities, rooftop gardens and parks can become safe homes for bees.

Protecting bees means protecting our own future. These tiny insects do a giant job for the planet.

What is the main idea of the passage?
options: B. The importance of bees and threats they face
C. How to keep bees at home
questions.explain: Cả bài nói vai trò của ong, nguyên nhân suy giảm và cách bảo vệ.

Read the following passage and mark the letter A, B, C, or D to indicate the best answer to each question.

Bees play a vital role in nature. They carry pollen from flower to flower, helping plants produce fruits and seeds. Without bees, many of the foods we love - apples, strawberries, and coffee - would disappear.

Sadly, bee numbers are falling around the world. Scientists believe several factors are responsible. Pesticides used on farms can poison bees. Climate change disrupts the timing of flowering, leaving bees without food. Diseases spread quickly among bee colonies kept close together.

The decline of bees affects humans directly. Farmers may produce less food, and prices could rise. Some regions already hire people to pollinate fruit trees by hand - a slow and costly job that bees once did for free.

Fortunately, we can help. Planting flowers that bloom in different seasons gives bees food all year. Avoiding pesticides in gardens protects them. In cities, rooftop gardens and parks can become safe homes for bees.

Protecting bees means protecting our own future. These tiny insects do a giant job for the planet.

Which of the following is NOT true?
options: A. Hand pollination is cheap and fast
B. Bees help plants produce fruits
C. Climate change affects flowering time
D. Bee numbers are falling worldwide
questions.explain: Bài viết thụ phấn bằng tay 'slow and costly' - chậm và tốn kém, không rẻ và nhanh.

questions.subject: ANH
questions.q:
Read the following passage and mark the letter A, B, C, or D to indicate the best answer to each question.

Many of us cannot imagine life without our phones. We check messages during meals, scroll through feeds in bed, and feel anxious when the battery is low. Experts call this 'phone addiction', and it is becoming more common among teenagers.

Too much screen time brings real problems. Studies link heavy phone use to poor sleep, tired eyes, and less time for exercise. It can also harm relationships: when everyone stares at their own screen, family conversations disappear. Some teens admit they feel stressed when they cannot check their phones for just one hour.

A 'digital detox' - a short break from devices - might be the answer. During a detox, people turn off non-essential apps, leave phones in another room, and rediscover offline activities like reading, sports, or chatting face to face. Even a one-day detox each week can make a big difference.

Schools in some countries have started 'phone-free days' with positive results. Students report better concentration and happier moods. Teachers notice livelier classroom discussions.

You do not need to throw away your phone to benefit. Start small: no phones at dinner, no scrolling before bed. As one expert puts it, 'Technology should serve us, not control us.'

What is the passage mainly about?
options: C. The problem of phone addiction and the idea of digital detox
D. How to buy a new phone
questions.explain: Bài nói về nghiện điện thoại, tác hại và giải pháp 'digital detox'.

questions.subject: ANH
questions.q:
Read the following passage and mark the letter A, B, C, or D to indicate the best answer to each question.

Oceans cover more than 70 percent of the Earth's surface. They give us food, oxygen, and regulate the climate. Millions of people earn their living from fishing and tourism related to the sea.

However, our oceans are in danger. Every year, about 8 million tons of plastic enter the oceans. Sea turtles mistake plastic bags for jellyfish, their favorite food, and many die. Oil spills from ships also kill thousands of sea birds and fish.

Overfishing is another serious problem. Modern ships can catch huge numbers of fish in a short time, leaving too few for the future. Some species, like bluefin tuna, are now at risk of disappearing.

There is still hope. Many countries have created marine protected areas where fishing is limited. People are also inventing new ways to clean plastic from the sea. In Vietnam, young volunteers regularly organize beach clean-ups.

The ocean's future depends on our actions today. If we reduce plastic use and fish responsibly, our blue oceans can recover and thrive again.

What is the main idea of the passage?
options: A. Threats to oceans and efforts to protect them
C. How to catch bluefin tuna
D. Why tourists love the sea
questions.explain: Bài nêu các mối đe dọa đại dương và nỗ lực bảo vệ.

Read the following passage and mark the letter A, B, C, or D to indicate the best answer to each question.

Many people think starting a business is only for adults, but a growing number of teenagers are proving them wrong. These young entrepreneurs are turning hobbies and ideas into real businesses while still at school.

Seventeen-year-old Khoa from Da Nang started making handmade soap during the lockdown. He posted photos online, and orders soon poured in. Now he employs three friends part-time and earns enough to pay for his own studies. 'I learned more from my small business than from any textbook,' Khoa says.

Sixteen-year-old Mai Anh from Hanoi loves baking. She began selling cookies to classmates, then expanded to an online shop. Her secret? 'I listen to customers and always try to improve,' she explains.

Experts say teen businesses teach valuable lessons: managing money, solving problems, and dealing with failure. Not every idea succeeds, but each attempt builds confidence and skills for the future.

Schools can support this trend by offering basic business courses and organizing fairs where students can sell their products. Parents, too, play an important role by encouraging creativity rather than focusing only on exam scores.

The stories of Khoa and Mai Anh show that age is just a number. With passion, effort, and a good idea, teenagers can achieve remarkable things.

What is the passage mainly about?
options: A. The history of online shops
C. Teenagers successfully running their own businesses
D. How to make handmade soap
questions.explain: Bài kể về các teen khởi nghiệp thành công và bài học từ đó.

Read the following passage and mark the letter A, B, C, or D to indicate the best answer to each question.

Music is a universal language that everyone can understand. Whether it is a lively pop song or a gentle lullaby, music has the power to change our mood. Scientists have found that listening to music we love releases chemicals in the brain that make us feel happy.

Music also helps us learn. Many teachers use songs to help students remember vocabulary and grammar. A catchy melody can make new words stick in our memory much longer than silent reading. This is why children learn the alphabet through the ABC song.

Playing an instrument brings even more benefits. Studies show that children who learn music often do better in maths and reading. Playing in a band or orchestra also teaches teamwork and discipline, as everyone must practise regularly and listen to each other.

In hospitals, music is used to help patients feel calmer and recover faster. Elderly people with memory problems often remember old songs even when they forget other things.

From classrooms to hospitals, music proves its value every day. As the famous saying goes, 'Where words fail, music speaks.'

What is the main idea of the passage?
options: A. Why pop songs are popular
B. The benefits of music in life
C. How to play the piano
questions.explain: Cả bài nói về lợi ích của âm nhạc: tâm trạng, học tập, sức khỏe.

Read the following passage and mark the letter A, B, C, or D to indicate the best answer to each question.

Vietnam is famous for its rich cultural heritage: ancient temples, traditional festivals, folk songs, and delicious cuisine. These treasures connect us to our ancestors and give us a sense of identity. However, rapid modernization is putting many of them at risk.

In big cities, old houses are being replaced by tall buildings. Traditional crafts, such as pottery and weaving, are disappearing because fewer young people want to learn them. Some folk songs are known only to elderly villagers.

Fortunately, efforts to preserve heritage are growing. The government has recognized many sites as national treasures and invested in their restoration. Festivals like Hue Festival and Hoi An Lantern Festival attract millions of visitors each year, showing that tradition can thrive alongside modern life.

Young people also play a key role. Many students now join clubs that teach traditional music and dance. Social media, surprisingly, has become a powerful tool for heritage: short videos of ao dai, water puppetry, and village festivals reach millions of viewers worldwide.

Technology offers more solutions. 3D scanning creates digital copies of ancient buildings, protecting them even if the originals are damaged. Online museums let people explore heritage from home.

Our heritage is a gift from the past and a promise for the future. Protecting it is everyone's responsibility.

What is the passage mainly about?
options: A. How to build tall buildings
B. Why young people dislike festivals
D. Efforts to preserve Vietnam's cultural heritage
questions.explain: Bài nói về di sản văn hóa Việt Nam đang bị đe dọa và nỗ lực bảo tồn.

Fortunately, efforts to preserve heritage are growing. The government has recognized many sites as national treasures and invested in their restoration. Festivals like Hue Festival and Hoi An Lantern Festival attract millions of visitors each year, showing that tradition can thrive alongside modern life.

Young people also play a key role. Many students now join clubs that teach traditional music and dance. Social media, surprisingly, has become a powerful tool for heritage: short videos of ao dai, water puppetry, and village festivals reach millions of viewers worldwide.

Technology offers more solutions. 3D scanning creates digital copies of ancient buildings, protecting them even if the originals are damaged. Online museums let people explore heritage from home.

Our heritage is a gift from the past and a promise for the future. Protecting it is everyone's responsibility.

In busy cities full of concrete and traffic, parks are like green lungs. They give residents fresh air, shade, and a peaceful place to relax. Children play there, elderly people exercise there, and families have picnics on weekends.

Parks also help the environment. Trees in parks absorb carbon dioxide and release oxygen. They lower the temperature of surrounding areas, fighting the 'heat island' effect that makes cities hotter than the countryside. During heavy rain, park soil absorbs water and reduces flooding.

Moreover, parks bring people together. Free concerts, outdoor yoga classes, and weekend markets often take place in parks. Neighbors who might never talk otherwise become friends through these activities.

Sadly, many cities lack enough parks. As land prices rise, green spaces are replaced by shopping malls and offices. Experts warn that cities need at least 9 square meters of green space per person, but many fall far short.

Protecting existing parks and creating new ones should be a priority. A city with more parks is not only more beautiful but also healthier and happier.

What is the main idea of the passage?
options: B. Why shopping malls are popular
C. The importance of parks in cities
questions.explain: Cả bài nói về vai trò của công viên: sức khỏe, môi trường, cộng đồng.

Parks also help the environment. Trees in parks absorb carbon dioxide and release oxygen. They lower the temperature of surrounding areas, fighting the 'heat island' effect that makes cities hotter than the countryside. During heavy rain, park soil absorbs water and reduces flooding.

Moreover, parks bring people together. Free concerts, outdoor yoga classes, and weekend markets often take place in parks. Neighbors who might never talk otherwise become friends through these activities.

Sadly, many cities lack enough parks. As land prices rise, green spaces are replaced by shopping malls and offices. Experts warn that cities need at least 9 square meters of green space per person, but many fall far short.

Protecting existing parks and creating new ones should be a priority. A city with more parks is not only more beautiful but also healthier and happier.

questions.explain: 'They' thay thế cho 'Trees in parks' ở câu trước.

The world of work is changing faster than ever. Robots and artificial intelligence are taking over repetitive tasks, from factory work to data entry. While some worry that machines will steal all jobs, experts see a different picture: new technology destroys some jobs but creates many others.

Jobs of the future will value creativity, critical thinking, and emotional skills - things machines cannot easily copy. Careers like AI engineer, data analyst, and renewable energy technician did not exist twenty years ago. Healthcare, education, and green technology are expected to grow strongly.

However, workers must prepare for this change. Learning one skill for life is no longer enough. People will need to retrain several times during their careers. Governments and companies are therefore investing in training programs to help workers adapt.

For students today, the message is clear: focus on learning how to learn. Strong basics in maths, science, and languages will always be useful. Equally important are soft skills like communication, teamwork, and problem-solving.

The future may seem uncertain, but it is also full of opportunity. Those who stay curious and keep learning will not just survive the changes - they will shape them.

What is the passage mainly about?
options: A. How technology is changing future jobs
B. How to become a technician
